intent: Pre-commit: tree-bound, retry-safe override approval (#35, #34 core)
notes: Phase 1 (#35 core, #34 changes 1-4). New starter `scripts/precommit_override.py`: the single interpreter for the override envelope (`gator-override-v2`). Per-worktree state under `git rev-parse --git-path gator-override` (block/approval/handoff JSON, atomic writes). Staged-change identity `index_tree()` = SHA-256 over `git ls-files --stage` minus hook-managed `.gator/` files (status.json, whiteboard.md, commit_issues.md, lint-allow.json, commit_draft.md), because validate stages those itself with timestamps and fixing a finding edits the draft. Unmerged index fails closed. Resolution classes approvable / lint / fix-required (unknown -> fix-required). Immutable approval snapshots; `inspect()` -> absent|malformed|expired|mismatch|premature|valid. 24 h expiry; the 10 s self-approval guard is kept. Sanitized override trailers.

`gator-pre-commit.py`: removed `check_override()`, `_write_override_request()`, `.override-meta.json`, and the `.gator/.override` bypass (now a `legacy-override-file` fix-required failure). `phase_validate()` evaluates every rule first, then applies an approval only for the exact staged change and only for its named approvable rules. It never consumes the approval: a retry blocked for another reason keeps it (the #35 bug). Every blocked attempt writes block.json with per-rule resolution; output tags each rule and names `gator hook approve` (not the stale script path). `commit-msg` reads the handoff for the current tree without consuming it and emits `Gator-Override-Approved-By/-Block/-Reason/-Rules`. `post-commit` `retire()`s all state (including abandoned and legacy v1 files). The commit_issues text points to `gator hook approve`.

`gator-approve.py`: argparse before prompts (#14). `status` / `approve` / `cancel`; no args or bare v1 flags -> approve. It always diagnoses: refuses with a specific reason for no block, malformed block, changed staged tree, expired block, nothing approvable (naming the fix-required rules), or a block younger than 10 s.

`gator-hook.py`: new `override` route (argv passthrough); `approve` is the alias for `override approve`. Both resolve the Git top level: runtime selection reads `<root>/.gator`, so from a governed subdirectory they were otherwise dispatched as ungoverned. This deliberately reverses the #32-era `approve` cwd pin; `enforcer-review` keeps the caller cwd.

Tests: new `tests/test_precommit_override.py` (28). Real-git lifecycle in temp repos: the #35 charter + invalid-change-type flow end to end, a nothing-approvable block is diagnosed, supersede matrix (modify/add/delete/rename, expiry, malformed, new rule, cancel), commit-msg failure keeps the approval for retry, trailer injection blocked, abandoned/legacy cleanup, legacy `.override` no longer authorizes, subdirectory and linked-worktree state, unmerged index, and units. `test_gator_hook.py`: HOOK_MAP now has 8 entries, the override route, and verb top-level resolution (the #32 `approve` pin is split).

Phase 1 review fixes: (P1) the outside-Git test uses `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, so it holds wherever pytest's basetemp lives. (P2) Block, approval, and handoff reads validate the full envelope and field types (`_BLOCK_FIELDS` / `_APPROVAL_FIELDS` / `_HANDOFF_FIELDS`, `_valid_failures`); a schema-valid partial or mistyped record is `malformed` and fails closed, never a hook traceback. 17 new cases, including 3 real-git hook runs.

Lint: `precommit_lint.run_layer1_lint()` no longer suppresses findings listed in the deprecated `.gator/lint-allow.json` (an unscoped (rule, file) bypass). Every finding is returned, tagged `allowlisted`. HIGH/CRITICAL findings are `lint`-class failures cleared only by an Architect approval for the exact staged change. `phase_validate()` warns `lint-allow-deprecated` and names listed findings that still block.
